name: Blockbuster
blurb: The giant US video rental chain, from one Dallas store in 1985 to one in Bend, Oregon
title: Blockbuster Video: What Happened and the Last Store in Bend
description: Blockbuster was the biggest video rental chain, with over 9,000 stores in 2004. It went bankrupt in 2010; one franchise in Bend, Oregon is still open.
answer: Blockbuster was a chain of video rental stores that opened its first shop in Dallas in 1985 and had more than 9,000 stores worldwide at its 2004 peak. Mail-order DVDs, then streaming, cheap retail DVDs and rental kiosks took its customers, and it filed for bankruptcy in 2010. Dish Network bought the brand in 2011 and closed the last company-owned US stores in early 2014. A single franchise store in Bend, Oregon is still open and has been the last Blockbuster in the world since 2019–2020.

body: A Blockbuster was a big, brightly lit shop with walls of VHS boxes (later DVD and game cases) sorted by genre and a wall of new releases. You took your pick to the counter with your membership card, paid for a rental of a few nights and brought it back before it was due, or paid a late fee. Stores also rented video games; Nintendo sued in 1989 to stop game rentals and lost.

The first store, which David Cook opened in Dallas on October 19, 1985, started with about 8,000 VHS and 2,000 Beta tapes. Under Wayne Huizenga, who took over from 1987, the chain expanded fast, opened its first UK store in London in 1989, and was bought by Viacom in 1994 for $8.4 billion.

body: Blockbuster's model depended on people driving to a store, and on late fees when they were slow to come back. Netflix's DVDs by mail had no store and no late fees; Walmart and other big retailers outsold it on DVDs; rental kiosks undercut it on price; and finally streaming removed the trip altogether. Blockbuster did start its own online rental service in 2004 and dropped late fees in 2005, but by its 2010 bankruptcy it owed about $900 million.

The Bend store opened in 1992 as part of a small Oregon chain, Pacific Video, and became a Blockbuster franchise in 2000. It is independently owned and licenses the name from Dish, which no longer grants new franchises. After the other franchises closed it became a tourist stop: it hosted Airbnb sleepovers for local guests in September 2020, starred in the 2020 documentary The Last Blockbuster and inspired the 2022 Netflix sitcom Blockbuster. By 2024 most of its income reportedly came from selling Blockbuster merchandise rather than rentals. It was still open as of 2026.

faq.a: The company went bankrupt in 2010, and Dish closed its last company-owned US stores between November 2013 and January 2014. One franchise store in Bend, Oregon is still open.

faq.q: Did Blockbuster really have the chance to buy Netflix?
faq.a: Yes. In 2000 Blockbuster declined an offer to buy Netflix for $50 million.

faq.q: Who owns the Blockbuster name now?
faq.a: Dish Network, which bought it out of bankruptcy in 2011. The Bend store licenses the name from Dish.
